answer: Every trust edge expires unless fresh work renews it within a set number of epochs, and each renewal signs a new nonce so an old approval cannot be replayed. The cipher on an edge is the pair of public keys, not a name, so renaming an alias inherits nothing. A garden of stale edges feeds nobody. Blunt: a farm has to keep producing real jobs to keep its web alive, and a walnut of an account with no output decays to zero weight before it can cash out, so holding a thousand identities costs a thousand live work streams.
